description: This Kotlin source file defines classes and functions for handling photo retrieval from device storage, including permission checks, querying media store for the latest photos, resizing images, encoding them into JPEG with size constraints, and preparing JSON responses. It encapsulates the logic within an Android app for efficiently fetching and encoding recent photos.

classes.name: PhotosLatestRequest
classes.description: Data class representing parameters for requesting latest photos including limit, maximum width, and quality.

classes.name: EncodedPhotoPayload
classes.description: Data class representing the photo data payload, including format, base64 encoded string, dimensions, and creation time.

classes.name: PhotosDataSource
classes.description: Interface defining methods to check permission and retrieve latest photos.

classes.name: SystemPhotosDataSource
classes.description: Singleton object implementing PhotosDataSource to fetch photos from system media store, handle permissions, decode, resize, encode images, and manage photo query logic.

classes.name: PhotosHandler
classes.description: Main class to handle photo requests, process parameters, check permissions, fetch and encode photos, and generate JSON responses.

methods.name: handlePhotosLatest
methods.description: Main method to process photo fetch request, check permissions, parse parameters, fetch photos, and create JSON response.

methods.name: parseRequest
methods.description: Helper method to parse JSON string into PhotosLatestRequest with default values and validation.

methods.name: queryLatestRows
methods.description: Queries the media store for the latest photos up to a specified limit.

methods.name: decodeScaledBitmap
methods.description: Decodes and scales a bitmap image from a URI to a specified maximum width.

methods.name: computeInSampleSize
methods.description: Calculates the sampling size for image decoding based on image width and target max width.

methods.name: encodeJpegUnderBudget
methods.description: Encodes a bitmap into JPEG format, adjusting quality and size to stay within character count limits.
